assessments.task_description:
Digital exam on concepts, principles and applied problems related to course lectures from weeks 1-8. This exam will be done through Blackboard.

Attempt period: opens 6am 25th September and closes 4pm 25th September - Once started exam time is 90 minutes

The digital exam is comprised of these question types:

i) Higher order thinking quiz questions to draw connections on principles, interpret case data examples, and understand concepts.

ii) Short essay questions to demonstrate understanding of course content.

iii) Multiple-choice questions related to courses readings and lectures.

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT)

assessments.task_description:
Small project to solve a geographical inquiry-driven problem using geospatial data and analysis completed in a Python notebook. Options given to do project related to an urban or physical geography topic. The expectation is that students select a premise and investigate an issue for a selected study area. The project is submitted as report following IMRaD structure and is accompanied with Python notebook file with worked analysis. Marked on criteria for structured answer, programming practice, and worked example.

On project completion students are assigned to a team to present their premise and findings on project topic. This forms part of an oral peer-review where teams cross-examine each other while defending their own work. It is moderated by course staff to confirm authorship and check project understanding. This is evaluated and may be used to adjust the project marking.
